title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
claim: In ε-Keggin zeolitic octahedral metal oxides, subatomic changes in linkers and extra-framework cations retune micropore openings and can invert or enhance CO2 versus C2H2 selectivity through size sieving.
explanation: A series of covalently linked ε-Keggin molybdate frameworks adjusts microporosity as elemental composition changes. NH4–ZM adsorbs little C2H2 and is used for CO2/C2H2 separation. Frameworks with Mg2+ or Zn2+ as both cations and linkers trap CO2 more strongly than C2H2, and the authors attribute separation to size sieving at the pore openings rather than to a change of the overall topology.
scope: ε-Keggin POM-based zeolitic octahedral metal oxides (ZOMO), including NH4–ZM, NH4–MM, NH4–NM, and NH4–IM and cation variants.
conditions: CO2 and C2H2 isotherms at 273 K; selectivity estimated by IAST.
caveats: The selectivity rule is drawn from this ZOMO series. Some members are noted as stable at high temperature and humidity, but adsorption data are not claimed for every composition under all conditions.
